summary: XRD analysis across the figures demonstrates that anion exchange in CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, I) nanocrystals (NCs) results in systematic, continuous shifts of diffraction peaks, consistent with homogeneous halide incorporation and retention of the cubic perovskite phase. Both direct anion exchange and interparticle exchange (mixing NCs of different halide compositions) yield single-phase materials with lattice parameters intermediate between the parent compounds, indicating effective and uniform anion exchange. No evidence of phase segregation or secondary phases is observed. However, quantitative crystallite size and microstrain information are limited by the absence of FWHM data.
experimental_variables: Degree of anion exchange (pristine, partially exchanged, fully exchanged)
Mixing of NCs with different halide compositions (interparticle exchange)

key_findings.finding: XRD peaks shift to higher angles with increasing Cl content and to lower angles with increasing I content, indicating lattice contraction and expansion, respectively.
All samples, including pristine, partially, and fully exchanged NCs, exhibit broad peaks consistent with nanocrystalline cubic perovskite phases.
Mixed NC samples (via interparticle exchange) show XRD peaks at positions intermediate between those of the parent NCs, suggesting homogeneous halide distribution and single-phase formation.

scientific_interpretation.claim: Anion exchange reactions in CsPbX3 NCs result in continuous, tunable lattice parameter changes without altering the cubic perovskite phase.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: Both figures show systematic peak shifts with halide composition, and captions/text state that the cubic phase is retained throughout exchange.

citations.evidence: Peaks shift to higher angles with Cl- incorporation; Peaks shift to lower angles with I- incorporation
Anion exchange reactions did not alter the crystal phase of the NCs (see Figures 3D , S4B and S9 )
Peak positions shift progressively from CsPbCl3 to CsPbBr3 to CsPbI3 NCs

scientific_interpretation.claim: Interparticle anion exchange (mixing NCs of different halide compositions) leads to homogeneous halide redistribution and formation of single-phase NCs with intermediate lattice spacings.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The caption and text explicitly state that mixed samples show XRD patterns compatible with single-phase NCs with average unit cell spacings intermediate between parent particles.

citations.evidence: XRD patterns were indeed compatible with single phase NCs with average unit cells spacings that were intermediate between those of the parent particles.
Mixed samples show peaks at intermediate positions between parent NCs

scientific_interpretation.claim: No evidence of phase segregation or secondary phases is observed in any of the XRD patterns, supporting the conclusion of complete or near-complete anion exchange.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: All XRD patterns show single sets of broad peaks without additional features that would indicate phase segregation.

citations.evidence: All samples show single sets of broad peaks; no secondary peaks reported.
